Draw a pedigree in an app, from a file, with no code

Source: R/runPedigreeApp.R
runPedigreeApp.Rd

Starts a small app in the web browser that opens a pedigree file and draws it with drawPedigreeDiagram, for someone who keeps a pedigree in a spreadsheet and does not write R. The call waits until the app is closed (press Escape or Ctrl-C in R, or stop the R session).

Usage

runPedigreeApp(ped = NULL, port = NULL, launch.browser = interactive())

Arguments

ped

NULL, or a data frame with the columns id, sire, dam and sex (its other columns kept), opened in the app as if read from a file.

port

NULL, for a free port chosen by shiny, or the port, one whole number from 1 to 65535.

launch.browser

TRUE to open the app in the web browser, FALSE to print its address only. By default, TRUE in an interactive R session.

Value

What shiny::runApp() returns when the app is closed, invisibly.

Details

In the app:

  • Open a CSV or text file with one row per animal, or the sample pedigree (375 rhesus macaques), or the ped given here.

  • Say which columns are the animal's id, its sire, its dam and its sex. The app recognises pedkindraw's names and common others (ego, egoid, indid; father, fatherid, dadid; mother, motherid, momid; gender), whatever their case and with or without spaces, dots or underscores; the user can change each. Sex values m, f, h and u in any case, male, female, hermaphrodite and unknown, and 1 and 2 (male and female, as kinship2 and PLINK files code them) are read as M, F, H and U, and the app says so; any other value is drawn as unknown. Every other column is kept, so a column pedkindraw reads by name is drawn as a script draws it.

  • See the pedigree drawn on the Diagram tab, with gen added by findGeneration, laid out by makePedigreeMatingLayout. What the layout says (a warning, or an animal it leaves out) is shown under the count of animals drawn; when a pedigree cannot be drawn, the app says so. A sire or dam with no row of its own is added by addParents, and the app names it.

  • Choose the animals to draw: everyone; one family (from findPedigreeNumber, the families of two or more animals listed largest first); focal animals with their ancestors and descendants (trimPedigree and getDescendantPedigree), each other parent of a descendant drawn too, without its own parents; or focal animals' near relatives (getNearRelativePedigree, 3 by default). Type the focal animals' ids, or click an animal in the drawing to make it the focal animal (a repeated animal's symbol counts as the animal). With more than 1,000 animals chosen, the app asks before drawing them, which can take a minute or more.

  • See the records' problems on the Checks tab, from checkPedigree on the whole file, and the animals chosen on the Animals tab.

Requirements

The shiny package (install.packages("shiny")), checked before anything else.

See also

drawPedigreeDiagram, which draws the pedigree, and checkPedigree, which finds the records' problems.

Examples

# It starts an app and waits until it is closed, so it runs when typed in
# R, and not in R CMD check.
if (interactive() && requireNamespace("shiny", quietly = TRUE)) {
  runPedigreeApp()

  ped <- data.frame(
    id = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
    sire = c(NA, NA, "A", "A"),
    dam = c(NA, NA, "B", "B"),
    sex = c("M", "F", "F", "M")
  )
  runPedigreeApp(ped)
}
